blocks.content: So how do you avoid that situation?
How do you make sure you don't lose a working version just because one change went wrong?
With Git, you can save your project at specific moments. Each save captures everything exactly as it is at that point.

blocks.alt: A video game save screen showing multiple named save slots with timestamps

blocks.content: If something breaks later, you don't try to fix it blindly or rebuild from memory. You simply go back to a version that was working.
That changes how you work. You stop hesitating before making changes, and you become more comfortable trying things out because you know your progress is safe.
That's the core idea behind Git.
👉 Next, you'll see where these saved versions are stored and how Git keeps track of them.
